owner_and_capability: Identity & Access — the behaviour suites (identity-access: modules/identityaccess/behavior, e2e-test in both test scopes) stop importing the refresh rotation application auth/rotation (identity-access/application), as ADR 0053 point 7 decides. The recovery proof becomes an input of the public refresh capability: identityaccess.AccountAuthentication.RefreshTokenWithAudit takes it as a parameter, modules/identityaccess/compose binds it to the request context for the rotation policy, and the account refresh route passes the X-Refresh-Recovery-Proof header on instead of binding it itself.
affected_tables: No table: the recovery proof reaches the same rotation policy with the same hash; auth.tokens is read and written as before.
atomic_cutover: No policy epoch and no new rule. RefreshTokenWithAudit on AccountAuthentication, Module and the compose engine gains a recoveryProof parameter after the refresh token; the compose engine calls rotation.WithRecoveryProof on it, which is what the account refresh route did before, so the application layer, its singleflight key and the stored proof hash are unchanged. The route passes r.Header.Get(rotation.RecoveryProofHeader). The four recovery suites in auth_core_test.go pass their proof through the public capability; the suites that refreshed without a proof pass an empty one, which leaves the context unbound as before. auth_switch_tenant_retire_test.go and auth_core_test.go assert against a local five-minute recoveryGrace, token_revocation_audit_test.go computes the sha256 hex fingerprint locally. The operator refresh route keeps binding its proof itself; its suites do not import auth/rotation. One key falls (46 -> 45), the last one on #3446. No route, header, status code, error string, table or write owner changes.
